# Incident Report — MTA 2024-07-30 Traffic Analysis Exercise

## Victim Host
| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 | 172.16.1.66 |
| MAC | 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08 |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-SKBR25F (domain: wiresharkworkshop.online) |
| Logged-in user | ccollier |

Grounded in: NBNS name responses (`DESKTOP-SKBR25F<00>/<20>` from 172.16.1.66), Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString` fields (`ccollier`, `DESKTOP-SKBR25F$` from 172.16.1.66 to DC 172.16.1.4), ARP (172.16.1.66 ↔ 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), and the malware's own beacon string (below), which self-reports hostname/user/OS.

Domain controller for context: 172.16.1.4 (WIRESHARK-WS-DC, MAC 5c:f9:dd:8c:97:35).

## Malware Family
**STRRAT** — **signature-confirmed**. TCP stream 83 (172.16.1.66:49754 → 141.98.10.79:12132) contains a repeating plaintext, pipe-delimited "ping" beacon that names the malware explicitly:

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|<uptime>
```

Fields decode to: literal family name `STRRAT`, victim/bot ID `1BE8292C`, hostname, username, OS, architecture, installed AV, STRRAT client version `1.6`, geolocation, persistence status, and an incrementing uptime counter (beacon interval ≈5 seconds, matching classic STRRAT heartbeat behavior).

## Indicators of Compromise

| Type | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| C2 endpoint | `141.98.10.79:12132` | TCP stream 83; plaintext STRRAT beacon protocol, first SYN at capture-relative time 76.99s, persists to end of capture with ~5s heartbeats |
| Supporting host | `208.95.112.1` (ip-api.com) | Plaintext `GET /json/` returning JSON geolocation (`countryCode: US`) that matches the `US:United States` field embedded in the STRRAT beacon — used by the implant to populate its own check-in data |

No transferred payload file name or SHA256 hash could be grounded: the initial delivery/dropper traffic is not visible in plaintext anywhere in this capture. In the ~60-70s window immediately preceding the first C2 connection, the host made TLS-encrypted connections to `github.com` (140.82.113.3), `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.110.133), `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209, SNI), and `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com` (23.194.164.136, SNI) — plausible infrastructure for staging a Java-based RAT like STRRAT — but since all of it is TLS-encrypted, no domain, URL, file name, or hash can be confirmed malicious from this capture. Do not treat these as confirmed IOCs.

## Benign Context (do not treat as malicious)
Extensive background traffic to Microsoft telemetry/services (`*.msn.com`, `*.microsoft.com`, `login.microsoftonline.com`, `office.com`/`officeapps.live.com` endpoints), Bing, Skype, Windows Update/WNS, and standard AD/domain traffic (Kerberos, LDAP, CLDAP, SMB2, DCE/RPC, NBNS, mDNS, LLMNR, SSDP) to/from the DC 172.16.1.4 — all normal enterprise Windows 11 / AD-joined workstation noise, unrelated to the compromise.

## Incident Summary
The Windows 11 workstation DESKTOP-SKBR25F (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as domain user ccollier, is infected with the STRRAT remote access trojan (bot ID 1BE8292C). The implant established a persistent plaintext C2 channel to 141.98.10.79 on TCP port 12132, sending periodic pipe-delimited "ping" beacons that self-identify the malware, host, user, and AV state, and separately queried ip-api.com to populate its own geolocation field. The initial infection/delivery vector is not observable in this capture because all candidate delivery traffic (GitHub, Maven Central, Oracle Java download infrastructure) occurred over TLS.
